content.text:
I can narrow this down much better if you tell me your **budget** and whether it’s for **school/work, gaming, travel, coding, or photo/video editing**. But based on current U.S. online deal roundups I found, these look like the strongest picks right now:

## Best laptop deals I’d check first — June 7, 2026

| Best for | Deal | Why it’s worth considering |
|---|---:|---|
| **Cheap everyday Windows laptop** | **Dell 15 Core 3 100U — $380** | Solid budget basics: 15.6" 1080p 120Hz IPS display, 8GB RAM, 512GB SSD, Windows 11. Better “safe buy” than many no-name ultra-cheap laptops. ([dealnews.com](https://www.dealnews.com/c49/Computers/Laptops/)) |
| **Very low price / lots of RAM** | **RNRUO 14" Pentium Gold, 32GB RAM / 512GB SSD — $299 at Walmart** | Huge RAM/storage for the price, but the Pentium Gold 6500Y is weak; I’d only buy this for browsing, documents, streaming, and light office work. ([dealnews.com](https://www.dealnews.com/c49/Computers/Laptops/)) |
| **Big screen budget laptop** | **HP 17.3" Intel Core Ultra 5 — $499.99 at HP** | Large 17.3" display and newer Core Ultra 5 chip, but only 8GB RAM and 256GB SSD; good if screen size matters more than portability. ([dealnews.com](https://www.dealnews.com/c49/Computers/Laptops/)) |
| **Productivity / heavy multitasking** | **Dell Inspiron 15 3530, i5, 32GB RAM / 1TB SSD — $799.99 at Amazon** | Strong for office work, coding, browser-tab overload, and multitasking; not for serious gaming because it uses integrated graphics. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/hardware/laptops/this-workhorse-laptop-with-32gb-ram-isnt-waiting-for-amazon-prime-day-as-its-now-usd300-off-to-help-you-clear-work-in-time-for-the-summer-holidays)) |
| **Best Mac deal under $1,000** | **13" M5 MacBook Air, 512GB — $949 at Amazon** | Good current Mac pick: newer M5 Air, $150 off, portable, strong battery life class. ([macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/guide/macbook-pro-air-deals/)) |
| **Cheapest MacBook** | **MacBook Neo — $589.99** | Apple’s new low-cost MacBook; small discount, but the base price is the main appeal. Best if you want macOS cheaply. ([macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/guide/macbook-pro-air-deals/)) |
| **Entry gaming** | **HP Victus RTX 4050 — $899.99 at Best Buy** | About the lowest I’d go for a new gaming laptop; RTX 4050 is entry-level but much better than integrated graphics. ([gamesradar.com](https://www.gamesradar.com/cheap-gaming-laptop-deals-190221/)) |
| **Best midrange gaming value** | **Alienware 16 Aurora RTX 5060 — $1,249.99 at Dell** | $600 off; good step up from RTX 4050/5050-class machines. ([gamesradar.com](https://www.gamesradar.com/cheap-gaming-laptop-deals-190221/)) |
| **Best gaming specs/value** | **Gigabyte Aero X16 RTX 5070, 32GB RAM / 1TB SSD — $1,389.99 at Best Buy** | Stronger GPU plus 32GB RAM and 1TB SSD; one of the better spec-per-dollar gaming picks. ([gamesradar.com](https://www.gamesradar.com/cheap-gaming-laptop-deals-190221/)) |
| **Premium thin gaming/OLED** | **Asus ROG Zephyrus G16 RTX 5070 OLED — $1,574.99 at Best Buy** | More premium build and display: 240Hz 2.5K OLED, RTX 5070, 1TB SSD. Good if you want gaming power without a bulky chassis. ([gamesradar.com](https://www.gamesradar.com/cheap-gaming-laptop-deals-190221/)) |

## My quick recommendations

- **Under $400:** Get the **Dell 15 Core 3 for $380** over the no-name 32GB RAM models unless you’re comfortable with compromises.
- **Best general-purpose Windows pick:** The **Dell Inspiron 15 with 32GB RAM / 1TB SSD for $799.99** is good if you multitask heavily.
- **Best Mac pick:** **M5 MacBook Air 13" for $949**.
- **Best gaming value:** **Gigabyte Aero X16 RTX 5070 for $1,389.99**.
- **If you can wait:** Amazon Prime Day is scheduled for **June 23–26, 2026**, so laptop prices may improve later this month. ([windowscentral.com](https://www.windowscentral.com/hardware/laptops/this-workhorse-laptop-with-32gb-ram-isnt-waiting-for-amazon-prime-day-as-its-now-usd300-off-to-help-you-clear-work-in-time-for-the-summer-holidays))

## What I’d avoid

- **Windows laptops with only 4GB RAM** — too limiting.
- **1366×768 displays** — look for **1080p/FHD or better**.
- **No-name brands with old Celeron/Pentium chips** unless the price is extremely low and your needs are basic.
- **Gaming laptops under ~$700** unless they have a real RTX GPU; many cheap “gaming” laptops are just normal laptops with flashy branding.

If you give me your **max budget** and what you’ll use it for, I can pick the top 3 deals for you and tell you which one I’d buy.
